Definition: Moral rhetoric is language that frames issues, policies, groups, or events in terms of moral values, principles, or judgments - invoking conceptions of right and wrong, justice/injustice, fairness, equality, rights, dignity, freedom, virtue/vice, moral desert, compassion/suffering, or moral duties - rather than in purely technical, economic, administrative, or empirical terms.
